gen-mystery-quest-gf-alumni-sans-sc: Alumni Sans SC reads tight and tall, its lowercase towering over its own capitals while the stems outweigh the hairlines just slightly. Mystery Quest adds a bookish, nostalgic opening act with its compact ascenders.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-arsenal: Mystery Quest leaves an open jaw on every curved stroke, bookish and a touch nostalgic. Arsenal keeps its x-height close to the cap height and its letters snug, so extended text moves along smoothly.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-changa: Changa reads modern and clean, with a lowercase that stands about as tall as cast iron capitals. And Mystery Quest brings open-jawed curves and a bookish, nostalgic mood to counter that sturdiness.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-geist-mono: Structured and technical, Geist Mono sets fixed-width letters with big side gaps, while Mystery Quest curves in bookish, open-jawed shapes. Paragraphs in it march along like tidy lines of code.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-genos: Pressed tight, edges almost kissing: that's the look of Genos. Mystery Quest brings bookish, nostalgic curves with open jaws, while the sans-serif body keeps reading smooth since no bowl ever closes up.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-major-mono-display: Neon glass meets storybook: Mystery Quest brings the bookish, nostalgic curves. Major Mono Display is the sharper half, monospace letters drawn like outlines in one width, tube-like and technical.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-martian-mono: Mystery Quest is bookish and nostalgic, with open jaws on every curved stroke and compact ascenders. Martian Mono is all fixed-width, code-style letters, loosely spaced and generous in every curve.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-mitr: Nostalgic from the first line, Mystery Quest curves with open jaws and compact ascenders. And Mitr, a contemporary sans whose lowercase nearly matches its capitals, keeps long reading smooth and friendly.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-mukta-mahee: Mystery Quest opens every curve with a bookish, nostalgic jaw. Mukta Mahee takes over with chunky lowercase that stands tall, approachable and clean, so reading it for a while feels easygoing.
gen-mystery-quest-gf-play: Play is a sans-serif with little height difference between its cases and only a faint weight shift between upstrokes and downstrokes. Mystery Quest handles the storybook mood; Play handles the plain reading.
